subject: SQRT function
notes: NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION — the same shape already adjudicated for the two siblings RV-15.27.3-2 (FUNCTION E) and RV-15.73.3-2 (FUNCTION PI), both carried at NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION in the inventory today. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.84.4 "rounded to 113 significant bits in the significand"` -> OK §15.84.4 3). THE RULE'S PRECONDITION CANNOT HOLD IN THIS COMPILER: DataBinder.cs#BindDeclarations lines 318-320 reject the mode outright — Edition.Error("COBOL0806", "ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO §8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL") — and the defence is double, because NumericRenderer.cs#StandardDecimal (line 394) is `Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal or ArithmeticMode.Standard`, which excludes StandardBinary: even if the bind error were downgraded, the render lane taken would be the NATIVE binary64 one, not a 113-bit one. Nothing in the tree can compute a binary128 square root: there is no 113-bit carrier and `grep Sqrt src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/*.cs` is empty. WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A DEFECT: the standard itself classes the enabling clause as processor-dependent — Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim by me, `cite.py --check A.3 "The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor"` -> OK §A.3 2) — and Annex F.2 makes it an obsolete feature; the non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md line 45, '| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |'. That is the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set (D13), which is why I record NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION rather than NOT-IMPLEMENTED. BARE QUESTION: should §15.84.4 rule 3 be recorded as discharged by the existing Annex A.3 item-2 documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? One decision settles E, PI and SQRT together. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH ITS OWN SIBLING: the standard-DECIMAL rule §15.84.4 r2 is NOT discharged by any such licence — that mode is supported and its rule is DIVERGES (see RV-15.84.4-2), so answering this question does not close §15.84.4. EDITIONS DERIVED FROM THE CONSTRUCT REGISTRY, NOT FROM IntrinsicCatalog: ConstructRegistry.g.cs row 'arithmetic-standard-binary-2014' — introduced 2014, obsolete 2023 — so the rule cannot apply at 85 or 2002. TEST-REF DELIBERATELY EMPTY: the existing StandardDecimalTests coverage exercises the MODE rejection and never references SQRT or any returned value, so per the sibling's struck-test precedent it does not cover this rule; a test pinning that FUNCTION SQRT under STANDARD-BINARY is refused by name would be the honest cover. test-needed. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
